gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Delta caps each power bank at 100 Wh 'with no exceptions' and allows at most two. Delta keeps the 101–160 Wh airline-approval route for spare batteries only. That means a 146 Wh power bank such as the AOHi Starship 40,000 mAh is barred on Delta even if the passenger asks for approval.
standout_why: Pages compared: the FAA PackSafe pages (ranks 1–6; faa.gov returned 403 when I opened it, so I worked from ChatGPT's answer, which is drawn from them), the cited IATA guidance PDF (only its title and metadata could be read: 'Passengers travelling with lithium batteries', file dated 2026-03-31), IATA's batteries page, 49 CFR 175.10, and the cited American Airlines pages (aa.com returned 403; ChatGPT's answer says AA now enforces 100 Wh). ChatGPT's answer and the FAA/IATA/CFR pages give the generic 100–160 Wh 'airline approval' tier for power banks, so a shopper would think a 146 Wh bank can fly with approval. ChatGPT names only AA as enforcing 100 Wh. None of its results covers Delta's rule. Delta allows two power banks of up to 100 Wh each, no exceptions, none recharged on board and none in overhead bins, and its 101–160 Wh approval applies only to spare batteries. AA's 100 Wh enforcement was already in ChatGPT's answer, so this is partly known; the Delta rule and the power-bank-versus-spare-battery split are new.
decides: This confirms that the pick has to stay under 100 Wh. It also argues for moving the AOHi Starship 40,000 mAh (146 Wh) out of the main table, or labelling it 'not allowed on Delta (or American, per ChatGPT's reading of AA's page) even with approval'. The page's 'needs airline approval' label understates the limit. Separately, Anker's US URL for the A1340 27,650 mAh 250W, which the current page lists, now returns 404. Anker's US store is selling the Prime 26K 300W (A110A, 26,250 mAh / 99.75 Wh, $229.99, in stock) in its place.

findings.label: Delta power bank limit
findings.value: Each power bank may not exceed 100 Wh, 'with no exceptions'. No more than two power banks per person.
findings.source_title: Battery or Fuel-Powered Items | Delta Air Lines
findings.note: Quoted from Delta's page. The page shows no effective date.

findings.label: Delta spare (non-power-bank) battery limit
findings.value: Up to 160 Wh per battery. No more than two spares between 100 and 160 Wh. Up to 20 spares in total. Over 160 Wh prohibited.
findings.source_title: Battery or Fuel-Powered Items | Delta Air Lines
findings.note: Delta treats power banks separately from spare batteries. The 101–160 Wh allowance covers spares only, not power banks.

findings.label: Delta in-flight use and stowage of power banks
findings.value: Power banks must not be recharged on board, may not charge a device during taxi, take-off or landing, and may not go in an overhead bin (keep them under the seat in front or in the seatback pocket).
findings.source_title: Battery or Fuel-Powered Items | Delta Air Lines
findings.note: The page also says some countries and airlines set their own power bank limits and that South Korea can impose significant fines.

findings.label: Delta compatibility
findings.value: Not allowed on Delta: its 146 Wh is above Delta's 100 Wh power bank cap, which has no approval exception.
findings.source_title: Battery or Fuel-Powered Items | Delta Air Lines
findings.note: The 146 Wh figure is from our existing listing (aohi-starship-40000mah-140w). I could not re-open AOHi's page today (HTTP 429). Compared 146 Wh against the 100 Wh cap.
